title: Microsoft Purview: apply default SharePoint library labels to existing files (Worldwide)
summary: Hold: Microsoft documents a PowerShell command for labeling progress, but the controls table reports that automation is not documented. The summary also turns a Worldwide rollout listing into an unsupported exclusion of other clouds.

claims.claim: An auto-labeling policy can apply a SharePoint document library's default sensitivity label to eligible existing files.
claims.quote: To extend your default library label deployment to existing files, create an auto-labeling policy that applies the default sensitivity label from each selected SharePoint document library to eligible existing files at rest.

claims.claim: The feature is admin-opt-in and does not label existing files through this policy unless an administrator creates and enables it.

claims.claim: The capability is Worldwide only.
claims.quote: Searched: '559105 Worldwide GCC availability'; 'default SharePoint library Worldwide Purview'. Read MC1477181, both roadmap records, and apply-sensitivity-label-automatically. These list rollout scope or plans, not an explicit exclusion of every other cloud.

claims.claim: Automation for the row governing labeling progress and failures is not documented.
claims.quote: IncludeProgressFeedback specifies whether to include the labeling progress of files in SharePoint or OneDrive. ... the command shows the progress of files to be labeled, files labeled in the last 7 days, and total files labeled for enabled auto-labeling policies.
claims.fix: Set controls[2].api to kind 'powershell', call 'Get-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <policy> -IncludeProgressFeedback', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/exchange/get-autosensitivitylabelpolicy'. Append to its note: 'The PowerShell call reports labeling progress.' Replace the prose clause asserting no API for the review pages with 'Get-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <policy> -IncludeProgressFeedback reports labeling progress.' Add that reference to sources and keep the rendered table consistent. This reference supports progress reporting, not item-level failure details.
